name: Vanamamalai Perumal Temple, Nanguneri
deity: Vishnu as Vanamamalai Perumal (Thothadrinathan), seated with Sridevi and Bhudevi, with the Goddess Sirivaramangai Nachiyar
period: A Divya Desam of the Pandya country at Sirivaramangai, sung by Nammalvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Inscriptions from the 13th century, with later additions
summary: At Nanguneri, the Sirivaramangai of the Alvars, Vishnu sits enthroned as Vanamamalai Perumal with his two consorts and is bathed in oil each day — a Divya Desam of the Pandya country and seat of the Vanamamalai Mutt.

sections.history: Nanguneri, remembered in the hymns as Sirivaramangai, lies on the old road south from Tirunelveli towards Kanyakumari. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams of Pandya Nadu, sung by Nammalvar in his Thiruvaimozhi. The temple carries many inscriptions, the earliest of them from 1236 CE, and records of 1794 CE note a grant of lands to its mutt by the Nawab of the Carnatic. Nanguneri is the seat of the Vanamamalai Mutt, one of the principal Sri Vaishnava monasteries of the south, whose first Jeeyar was a foremost disciple of Manavala Mamunigal; the Jeeyars of the mutt have long been closely bound to the temple's worship.
sections.architecture: The sanctum is crowned by the Nandavardhana vimana. Within, Vanamamalai Perumal sits enthroned beneath the hoods of Adisesha, with Sridevi and Bhudevi seated on either side, so that the Lord appears as if holding court — a durbar form treasured by devotees. The Goddess Sirivaramangai Nachiyar has her separate shrine. The temple tank is the Chetruttamarai Theertham, and within the temple is the oil well, the Ennai Kinaru, into which the oil of the daily ablution is gathered.
sections.legends: Local tradition tells of a childless king who prayed to Vishnu and was led to Nanguneri. When he dug the earth here, blood welled up from the ground; he was told to bathe the Lord in oil every day, and the flow ceased. Blessed in time with children, the king raised the temple. The daily oil ablution continues, and the oil, gathered in the temple well, is given as prasadam and is deeply cherished by devotees.
sections.festivals: The chariot festival in the Tamil month of Chithirai is the temple's grandest celebration, among about a dozen annual festivals. Vaikunta Ekadashi and the days of Nammalvar are observed with devotion, with processions of the Lord and his consorts through Nanguneri. Confirm festival dates locally.
sections.experience: A Divya Desam with a living monastic tradition beside it: pilgrims come for the enthroned Lord and his consorts, and to receive the sacred oil. A short drive west brings one to Thirukkurungudi below the hills, and the two Divya Desams are often visited together.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Chithirai chariot festival and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Nanguneri is about 30 km south of Tirunelveli on the national highway to Kanyakumari and is reached easily by bus or car; it has a small railway station, with Tirunelveli the main junction. The nearest airports are Thoothukudi and Thiruvananthapuram.
